title: Whole Cherry Clafoutis
summary: Whole dark cherries baked in a light, puffy vanilla and lemon batter in a sugared dish, finished with a snow of icing sugar.
equipment: 24 cm round ovenproof dish or cast-iron pan

ingredients.item: soft unsalted butter, for the dish
sweet cherries, stems removed, pitted and left whole
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Prepare the dish
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan). Butter the dish generously and sprinkle with the tablespoon of sugar, which gives the edges a light caramelised crust. Spread the cherries over the base in a single layer.

steps.title: Whisk the batter
steps.text: Whisk the eggs and sugar until pale and foamy, then whisk in the flour and salt until smooth. Gradually add the milk, then the melted butter, vanilla and lemon zest; the batter should be thin, like a crêpe batter.

steps.title: Pour
steps.text: Pour the batter gently over the cherries so they stay in place.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 35-40 minutes, until puffed and golden at the edges and a knife in the centre comes out clean (the custard reaches at least 71 °C). It will sink as it cools; that is normal.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Cool for 15-20 minutes, dust with icing sugar and serve warm.

tips: A cherry pitter keeps the fruit whole and looking its best.
A common mistake is a thick batter; it should pour like single cream.
Bake in a dish that just fits the cherries in one layer.
Serve warm, as it is at its fluffiest soon after baking.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Cover and refrigerate for up to 2 days. Eat cold or warm gently in a low oven.
